title: A solid cylinder rolls off a vertical edge: rotation about the corner, energy with the parallel-axis inertia and the speed when it loses contact
summary: A steel cylinder rolls at v0 = sqrt(gR/3) to the edge of a block and turns about the corner. The corner's push shrinks as the centre swings down and reaches zero at cos(theta) = 5/7 - the run freezes there and measures v = sqrt(5gR/7), option B - then the cylinder flies off on a parabola. Change v0 and watch where it leaves.
subject: Physics
chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
topic: Rolling off a vertical edge - rotation about the corner, energy with the parallel-axis inertia, and loss of contact when N = 0
subtopics: Rolling without slipping: the contact point is at rest, so reaching the edge gives no impulse
Moment of inertia about the corner by parallel axes: I = I_cm + mR^2 = 3/2 mR^2
Energy about a fixed pivot: 3/4 m v^2 = 3/4 m v0^2 + mgR(1 - cos theta)
Radial equation at the corner: N = mg cos theta - m v^2/R; contact lost when N = 0
Leaving at once when v0^2 >= gR
concepts: At the edge the rolling cylinder's contact point is already at rest, so it simply starts turning about the corner with omega = v0/R
About the corner the kinetic energy is (1/2)(3/2 mR^2)(v/R)^2 = 3/4 m v^2
Energy: 3/4 v^2 = 3/4 v0^2 + gR(1 - cos theta)
The corner's push N = mg cos theta - m v^2/R falls as theta grows; contact is lost when v^2 = gR cos theta
cos theta = (3 v0^2/gR + 4)/7 = 5/7 for v0^2 = gR/3, so v = sqrt(5gR/7)
formulas: 3/4 m v^2 = 3/4 m v0^2 + mgR(1 - cos theta)
N = mg cos theta - m v^2/R

methods: Solved independently: no impulse at the edge, I_corner = 3/2 mR^2, energy about the corner with N = 0 gives cos theta = 5/7 and v^2 = 5gR/7 - option B
sympy: energy with the parallel-axis inertia and the contact condition give cos theta = (3 v0^2/gR + 4)/7 = 5/7; only option B matches
Newton-Euler in Cartesian coordinates (scipy), with the corner's force solved from the no-slip constraint and no energy equation: release at v^2/gR = 0.714286, cos theta = 5/7
Exact fractions: cos theta = 5/7, and the energy balance closes
Whole input range: v0^2/gR from 0.04 to 0.99 agrees with (3u + 4)/7; v0^2 >= gR leaves at the edge; after release the cylinder never touches the block again
Every option audited: A (0) and C (gR/15) are below v0^2 - impossible; D (3gR/7) would need cos theta = 3/7 where N = -2/3 mg (the initial KE subtracted); B is the only consistent one
